business_problem: Modjo's Atlas-backed conversational-intelligence platform was hitting 100% CPU saturation because inefficient connection handling, unclosed sessions, and large requests were driving performance bottlenecks and unnecessary infrastructure cost.
solution_summary: Modjo uses MongoDB Atlas as the operational database behind its conversational-intelligence platform, which ingests customer-call data from Zoom, Skype, and Google Meet and runs separate transcription and speaker-identification pipelines. Atlas stores orchestration state, logging, and next-step decisions; writes reach Atlas through a custom API built on AWS Lambda and API Gateway while downstream services read directly. As load grew, inefficient connection management, unclosed sessions, and large per-request datasets drove 100% CPU saturation on an oversized cluster. MongoDB Professional Services first reworked schema and indexing, then traced persistent hot spots to per-operation client creation and leaked sessions, guiding code changes that reused a single client and explicitly closed sessions after retrieval.

data_flow: Conversation data from Zoom, Skype, and Google Meet feeds Modjo's transcription and speaker-identification pipelines. Orchestrator services write task states and next-step decisions through AWS Lambda and API Gateway to MongoDB Atlas, while downstream services read Atlas directly to drive analytics and the end-user application.
business_outcome: After minor code changes, Modjo cut CPU usage from 100% to 20%, reduced query targeting from 40,000 to 1, downsized its Atlas cluster from M60 to M30, and lowered monthly Atlas costs by 75%.
